authority_notes: Plan-17 R1-R5 public-safe contracts only. The private target-binding production wrapper and core expose no arbitrary clock, factory, hook, test adapter or dependency-injection surface; tests import the production wrapper and use the real host clock. The default-OFF adapter derives its target map from Path Registry and requires a separately pinned writer-exclusive ACL admission before any enabled store mutation. That packet's control_root_ref must equal the shared map's canonical target.control logical ID exactly; pathref, binding or other syntactically valid refs are rejected before store creation. It also binds control identity, ACL readback, sole writer, wrong-writer denial, authority and host-clock validity. Every generation and active lineage carries the current Suite/9-target identity commitment, preventing cross-Suite transplant. Once a store has records, register pre-reads the active/prior generation authority before taking the lock, rejects caller-coordinated authority rotation, uses the stored lock-break authority, and rechecks the pointer/generation inside the lock. Revoked pointers persist both lock-break and reactivation authority; full-revoke reactivation is authorized by the stored revoked lineage, never the new candidate packet. Revoke follows the same pre-read/in-lock authority pattern. Lock-break and reactivation requests use trusted validity windows evaluated against host Date.now. Stable target/store-lane identities, fsynced temp plus atomic no-overwrite immutable publication, full revocation-head chain validation, max-generation epoch, explicit reactivation, atomic stale-lock preservation/compensation, and recursively value-checked path-free public receipts remain enforced. Enabled effects are confined to private control state below target.control; the other eight targets, payload, ACL state, services and tasks are not mutated.
